ability: What a card can do: a tap, a paid or a passive ability.
attack: Fighting a monster in a monster slot or from the monster deck.
bonus soul: A soul card beside the board that any player can earn.
character: The card a player plays as, like Isaac or Maggy.
counter: A token on a card, as a charge or a spider counter.
curse: A monster card that stays on a player and hurts them.
damage: What lowers health; a card or player with no health left dies.
deck: A face-down pile to draw from: loot, treasure, monster, room.
discard: The face-up pile beside a deck, and putting a card there.
eternal: An item a character starts with; it never leaves its owner.
health: How much damage a card or player can take; HP on the cards.
item: A treasure card in front of a player.
loot: The cards in a player's hand and their deck.
monster: A card to attack; killing it gives rewards and maybe a soul.
priority: Who may play or respond next while the stack resolves.
recharge: Making a used (turned) item usable again.
roll: Throwing the die; many cards trigger on a roll.
room: A card from the room deck that changes the rules while it is out.
shop: The treasure slots where a player buys items for 10¢.
soul: What players collect; four souls win the game.
stack: The list of plays and rolls waiting to resolve, last first.
treasure: The deck of item cards, and a card from it.
turn: One player's go: start, actions, end.
